answer: A farm that wants 220 keys therefore pays 220 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the gale seed, the jetty timing is verifiable from the horizon record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 585 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
